candidates.title: The Rain Gauge That Predicted a Flood
story_beats: At the snowy meadow, rabbit and fox discovered the school rain gauge reported twice as much rain as the nearby weather station before the library opened, leaving the visiting readers waiting.
Rabbit attempted an immediate fix, but they recalibrated the scale but the next shower produced another impossible reading; fox stopped the attempt before the situation worsened.
Fox examined the evidence and realized runoff splashing from the adjacent roof was entering the gauge funnel; together they revised their plan rather than repeating the mistake.

With the visiting readers watching, they moved the gauge to an unobstructed location and compared readings during the next shower, then explained the clue so their neighbors could prevent the problem next time.

candidates.title: The Bell That Rang With No Boat
story_beats: At the snowy meadow, rabbit and fox discovered the harbor bell rang every night although no boat approached the pier before the library opened, leaving the visiting readers waiting.
Rabbit attempted an immediate fix, but the watchkeeper replaced the bell rope but the sound returned at the next tide; fox stopped the attempt before the situation worsened.
Fox examined the evidence and realized a floating marker struck a loose metal bracket only when the tide reached its highest point; together they revised their plan rather than repeating the mistake.
With the visiting readers watching, they secured the bracket and marked the high-water hazard for the harbor crew, then explained the clue so their neighbors could prevent the problem next time.

candidates.title: The Clock That Cast Two Shadows
story_beats: At the snowy meadow, rabbit and fox discovered the town square sundial appeared to point to two different hours before the library opened, leaving the visiting readers waiting.
Rabbit attempted an immediate fix, but the caretakers repainted the hour markings but the conflicting shadows remained; fox stopped the attempt before the situation worsened.
Fox examined the evidence and realized a new mirrored shop window reflected sunlight onto the dial from the opposite direction; together they revised their plan rather than repeating the mistake.
With the visiting readers watching, they shielded the reflected beam and checked the dial against the actual sun, then explained the clue so their neighbors could prevent the problem next time.
